hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.b: British colonial expansion was driven by ((competition)) with other European powers such as Spain, France, Portugal and the Netherlands, as well as the desire for ((resources)) and new markets. With the support of the monarchy, England began establishing ((overseas)) trade networks in the 16th century.

hint.label: to repress vs. to oppress

atoms.b: In the 17th century, several colonial ((settlements)) were established along the North American Atlantic coast. The British Monarchs granted ((trading_companies)) and private actors the right to claim and exploit new territories. In turn, they began to displace indigenous populations. When resistance occurred, state armies ((intervened)) and repressed the resisting populations.

hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>foundation</lang> bedeutet Fundament. <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>loss</lang> bedeutet Verlust. <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>effort</lang> bedeutet Anstrengung, Bemühung, Leistung.
hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.b: Through ((colonial_wars)) with rival empires, England gained control over most of the North American colonies, islands in the Caribbean, slave trading post in West Africa and trading posts in India. When the United States gained ((independence)), the UK lost much of its North American territory, marking the end of the “First Empire”.
